title: Filling the gaps a satellite would leave
query: Infrared satellites cannot see the sea surface through cloud, so on a typical day a large part of a temperature image is missing. Treat the supplied GLORYS12 daily near-surface temperature for 1993-2020 in the western Tasman Sea off south-eastern Australia (46-26 S, 147-162 E) as the true ocean, remove data in patterns that resemble cloud cover, and reconstruct the missing values with at least two methods. Determine how the reconstruction error depends on the fraction and size of the gaps, the method, the season and the location, which features are lost first, and how the errors would bias averages and extremes computed from gap-filled fields. Cloud observations are not supplied; state how you chose the gap patterns and what that choice implies.

region.name: Tasman Sea and East Australian Current
